reason: Hardy's apparatus cross-references all four baptism accounts at this verse — Matthew 3:16, Mark 1:10, Luke 3:22, John 1:32 — which is the right thing for a study edition to do and leaves the catalogue's question unanswered. The wording answers it. 'The Holy Ghost descended' occurs in exactly one KJV verse, Luke 3:22; Matthew 3:16 reads 'the Spirit of God descending', Mark 1:10 'the Spirit like a dove descending', John 1:32 'the Spirit descending from heaven'. All three name the agent as Spirit, not Holy Ghost, and Matthew and Mark both place the participle before the dove where the Book of Mormon and Luke place it after the noun. Matthew 3:16 is additionally excluded on its own account: its distinctive material — the heavens opened unto him, the lighting upon him — is entirely absent here, though Matthew 3:14-15 IS the source at 31:5. The link is at Luke 3:22. Mark 1:10 and John 1:32 are excluded on the same evidence and are not given separate entries.

reason: The machine's top-scoring candidate for the verse at rarity 2.00, and the model case of the trap ADJUDICATING §4 names. Judges 9:48 is Abimelech on mount Zalmon, cutting a bough with an axe and laying it on his shoulder, telling his men 'What ye have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done' — after which they burn a thousand men and women alive in the tower of Shechem. 2 Nephi 31:12 is the Son of God saying 'follow me, and do the things which ye have seen me do'. The five-word run is exact and the referent could hardly be more opposed: an imitation that leads to a massacre against an imitation that leads to salvation. There is also no reason to think the Book of Mormon knows Judges 9 — nothing else in 2 Nephi touches it — whereas the imitation-of-Christ language of the verse is fully accounted for by John 13:15 and by the chapter's own 'he having set the example before them' at 31:9.

Proposed at both 31:13 and 31:14 at rarity 1.50, and it is the window closing one word early. Exodus 14:24 has the LORD looking through 'the pillar of fire and of the cloud'; 2 Nephi 31:13 has 'the baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost'. The shared string is a preposition, a noun, a conjunction and an article, and the word that decides the sense is the one on the far side of the window in each case — cloud there, Holy Ghost here. The real background of the phrase is Matthew 3:11 and Luke 3:16, both of which the Book of Mormon inverts (Holy Ghost first, then fire, in the KJV; fire first here), and that inversion is registered on the 1 Corinthians 13:1 link at this verse rather than given a row of its own, because it holds at 31:13, 31:14 and 31:17 alike and is Nephi's settled form rather than a fresh borrowing at each occurrence.

Covered in principle by the standing formulaic exclusion at 1 Nephi 1:5 and noted here only because the machine proposes it twice in these three chapters (31:19 and 32:9). 'Behold, I say unto you' is one of the Book of Mormon's commonest discourse markers and one of the KJV's; the harvest saying of John 4:35 has no other contact with either verse.

A six-word run and a Deuteronomic commonplace: 'keep the commandments of the LORD' recurs through Deuteronomy, Joshua, Kings and Chronicles, and 'keep the commandments' is used some sixty times in the KJV. 2 Nephi 31:10 has 'keep the commandments of the Father', which is the Johannine rather than the Deuteronomic object and belongs with John 15:10. The verse's link is to John 21:22, on the singleton 'follow thou me'.
